note: Container-operation walkthrough by an agent, not a human operator study. Commands ran against disposable Compose projects owned by this walkthrough. Secrets, cookies, mail bodies and links are not recorded; command output is reduced to exit codes and selected sanitized lines.

runs.note: The reviewer stopped this run while it waited for readiness after the failed up; the remaining steps ran in install-up.

steps.action: Check prerequisites: docker version, docker compose version, docker context show, Git and OpenSSL
steps.expected: Docker Engine and the Compose plugin answer, the context is the intended host, Git and OpenSSL are present.
steps.actual: Docker Engine 29.8.0, Compose 5.5.1, context "default" (the local host), git version 2.55.0 | OpenSSL 3.6.4 25 Aug 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 3.6.4 25 Aug 2026). Disk had about 1.5 TB free.

steps.action: Clone into a new directory, enter it, and select the documented revision
steps.expected: A detached checkout at 3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69.
steps.actual: git clone and git checkout --detach exited 0 in 3 s. HEAD is 3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69; 0 uncommitted paths.

steps.action: Run the grouped .env commands
steps.expected: .env exists with mode 600 and both keys generated.
steps.actual: The block exited 0. .env has mode 600. AUTH_SECRET and OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY each hold a different 44-character generated value (values not recorded).

steps.action: Run the grouped .env commands again over the existing .env
steps.expected: The commands refuse to overwrite the existing .env and stop before changing its keys.
steps.actual: The second run exited 1 with "bash: line 4: .env: cannot overwrite existing file". The .env bytes were unchanged (same SHA-256 before and after).

steps.action: Edit .env with the origin, port and project name, and create compose.operator.yml
steps.expected: Each setting appears once; compose.operator.yml names the two revision-tagged images.
steps.actual: Added COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=doc029-opinstall-r1, COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yml:compose.operator.yml, OPENLAW_BUILD_COMMIT=3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69, OPENLAW_BUILD_DIRTY=false, BASE_URL=https://openlaw-r1.localhost:23321 (the local proxy origin chosen for this check) and PORT=23320, each once. Wrote compose.operator.yml exactly as the article shows. Saving the keys in a secret store was represented by the private walkthrough directory outside the repository.

steps.action: Check the configuration: docker compose config --quiet and --services
steps.expected: config --quiet prints nothing and exits 0; the services are app, worker, postgres and doc-engine.
steps.actual: docker compose config --quiet exited 0 with no output. config --services listed app, doc-engine, postgres, worker.

steps.action: docker compose pull postgres
steps.expected: Postgres 16 is available.
steps.actual: docker compose pull postgres exited 0 in 1 s.

steps.action: docker compose build app doc-engine
steps.expected: Both images build and carry the revision tags; the worker needs no separate build.
steps.actual: docker compose build app doc-engine exited 0 in 17 s. openlaw-local:3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69 is sha256:1f6d836c747a2b5120bed65db3d33096b5a16392402a770ea99df67f1a17a903; openlaw-engine-local:3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69 is sha256:64d1f9448e278e3ce11e2d8d82462552109ee980cce8eae93c8a5561ce398b67.

steps.action: docker compose up -d --no-build --pull never, then docker compose ps
steps.expected: The four services start from the built images.
steps.actual: Check did not pass: up exited 1: Network doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-doc-engine Creating | Network doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-backend Creating | Network doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-backend Creating
steps.note: Environment, not the article: the Docker daemon on this shared host had no free address pool because parallel documentation labs held every default pool. Superseded by the install-up phase after the network workaround.

steps.action: Environment workaround: create the two project networks with explicit private subnets
steps.expected: The shared host's Docker address pools are exhausted by parallel labs; pre-created networks carrying the Compose project labels let the article's own up command proceed unchanged.
steps.actual: The first up failed with "all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted" because other parallel documentation labs hold every default pool. The reviewer created doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-backend internal=false 10.233.40.0/24; doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-doc-engine internal=true 10.233.41.0/24 with the Compose project and network labels (docker network create --subnet ... --label com.docker.compose.project=doc029-opinstall-r1 --label com.docker.compose.network=...). No installation file changed; this is a host workaround, not an article step.

steps.action: docker compose up -d --no-build --pull never, then docker compose ps
steps.expected: The four services start from the built images.
steps.actual: up exited 0. docker compose ps: app running; doc-engine running; postgres running; worker running.

steps.action: curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/readyz; check the worker is running and the document engine becomes healthy
steps.expected: readyz succeeds; worker running; doc-engine healthy.
steps.actual: curl --fail /readyz exited 0 with HTTP 200. The worker is running and the doc-engine reports healthy. The running app and worker containers use sha256:1f6d836c747a2b5120bed65db3d33096b5a16392402a770ea99df67f1a17a903; doc-engine uses sha256:64d1f9448e278e3ce11e2d8d82462552109ee980cce8eae93c8a5561ce398b67. Elapsed from the first prerequisite command to readiness: 120 s on this host (build cache warm from earlier labs of the same revision).

Caddy issues the localhost certificate from its internal CA; the browser context accepts that CA, which does not test public certificate issuance.

steps.action: Missing secret: blank AUTH_SECRET
steps.expected: Compose refuses before any container changes; restoring the key recovers.

Restoring the key made config --quiet exit 0; /readyz answered 200.

steps.expected: The start fails and names the port; the other listener is untouched; an unused port recovers.
steps.actual: With PORT=23326 held by an unrelated owned listener, up exited 1 with "Error response from daemon: failed to set up container networking: driver failed programming external connectivity on endpoint doc029-opinstall-r1-app-1 (7231d4cc5c93e96fe8dc720c9937ba1eecf36f6764a7be". docker compose ps then listed doc-engine, postgres. The unrelated listener still answered 200. Restoring PORT=23320 and running up -d --no-build --pull never brought the app back; /readyz 200.
steps.note: Passed, but the recorded line was cut before the port text. The port-negative rerun records the part of the message that names the port.

steps.action: Unavailable dependency: stop the bundled database
steps.expected: Readiness fails while the database is unavailable and recovers when it returns.
steps.actual: docker compose stop postgres; /readyz then answered 503. docker compose start postgres; /readyz answered 200 again.

steps.action: Negative: the authoring lab is not used as installation evidence

steps.actual: Every V-C44 step ran against doc029-opinstall-r1, built by the article's own clone, .env and Compose commands. No lab.mjs lab, seed data, or dev overlay was used.

steps.action: Occupied port: set PORT to a port an unrelated listener already holds

steps.action: docker compose restart does not apply a changed .env
steps.expected: After setting MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and restarting, the app still has the old environment.
steps.actual: After adding MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and docker compose restart app, the container's MAX_UPLOAD_MB was still empty and a 1,100,000-byte upload was accepted (201).

steps.action: up -d --no-build --pull never applies it; MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 refuses a larger upload and accepts a smaller one
steps.expected: The recreated app enforces the 1 MB ceiling.
steps.actual: up -d --no-build --pull never recreated the app; MAX_UPLOAD_MB is now 1 in the container. The 1,100,000-byte upload was refused with 413 "That file is over the 1 MB upload limit."; a 200,000-byte upload was accepted (201). The Caddy proxy has no body limit configured, so the app's own refusal was seen.

steps.action: An unreadable MAX_UPLOAD_MB falls back to the default instead of stopping startup
steps.expected: MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten starts normally and accepts a 1.1 MB upload.
steps.actual: With MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten the app started (/readyz 200) and accepted the 1,100,000-byte upload (201), so the ceiling fell back to the 100 MB default. The setting was then removed and the containers recreated.

steps.action: config --quiet validates without printing the expanded configuration
steps.expected: Exit 0 and no output.
steps.actual: docker compose config --quiet exited 0 and printed nothing on stdout or stderr.

steps.action: App and worker share image and configuration with different commands; the engine has no database or credential access; database and engine ports are unpublished; PORT moves only the host port

steps.actual: App and worker run the same image sha256:1f6d836c747a2b5120bed65db3d33096b5a16392402a770ea99df67f1a17a903 with commands ["node","apps/api/dist/index.js"] and ["node","apps/worker/dist/index.js"]. DATABASE_URL, STORAGE_PATH, BASE_URL, DOC_ENGINE_URL and OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY are identical in both (compared, not recorded). The doc-engine container has no DATABASE_URL, AUTH_SECRET or OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY and joins only doc029-opinstall-r1_openlaw-doc-engine. Postgres and doc-engine publish no host ports; the app maps container port 3000 to host port 23320.

steps.action: Document-engine defaults: DOC_ENGINE_URL and DOC_ENGINE_TMPFS_SIZE
steps.expected: The bundled engine URL is http://doc-engine:8080 and scratch space is a 2g tmpfs.
steps.actual: The app's DOC_ENGINE_URL is http://doc-engine:8080. The doc-engine mounts /tmp as tmpfs {"/tmp":"mode=1777,size=2g"} with a read-only root filesystem (true).

steps.action: No separate email Settings page after the wizard
steps.expected: Settings navigation offers no Email page; the Setup checklist Email row, if shown, has no link.
steps.actual: Settings -> Organization -> General shows 31 links (Skip to content, Help, Home, Inbox, My Tasks, Matters, Contracts, Documents, Entities, Knowledge, Auto-Docs, Profile, Appearance, Notifications, View Business Portal, General, Regions, Departments, Users, Matters, Contracts, Intake, Entities, Knowledge, Auto-Docs, Notifications, AI analysis, Integrations, Business-user portal, E-signature, AI analysis); none is for email or SMTP. The onboarding state's email step reads "email":{"done":true,"settingsPath":null}.

steps.action: Rotate OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY: set OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS to the current value and a new key, then recreate
steps.expected: The app reports re-encryption and the stored relay still sends.
steps.actual: Recreated with the previous key and a newly generated key. The app logged "Stored credentials resealed under the key in use: smtp_url (1).". A test send through the stored relay answered 200 and arrived.

steps.action: Remove OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS and recreate again
steps.expected: The stored relay still sends under the new key alone.
steps.actual: Removed OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS and recreated. Boot lines about stored credentials: none. A test send answered 200 and arrived.

steps.action: Mismatched key: a valid but wrong OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY
steps.expected: Records stay readable; the saved relay cannot be used; restoring the correct key and recreating recovers without re-entering the relay.
steps.actual: With a different valid key, /readyz answered 200 and the app logged "No configured key opens these stored credentials: smtp_url (1). They are left as they are, so they are still recoverable: boot once with the old key in OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS, or paste the credentials again in Settings.". The Contract list answered 200. Email source read "unset" and a test send answered 502 "The test email could not be sent. SMTP is not configured — save a relay first.". Restoring the retained key and recreating (without re-saving the relay) made the test send answer 200 and arrive.

steps.action: Missing or short OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY: both processes require it at startup
steps.expected: A blank key is refused by Compose; a short key stops app and worker startup; the correct key recovers.
steps.actual: A blank key made up exit 1 with "error while interpolating services.app.environment.OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY: required variable OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY is missing a value: OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY is required — generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32` and set it in .env". A 16-character key stopped startup: /readyz unreachable (ECONNRESET); app logged "OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY is shorter than 32 characters. Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32`."; worker logged "{"reason":"OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY is shorter than 32 characters. Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32`.","level":"error","time":"2026-09-1". Restoring the key recovered readiness and delivery.

steps.action: Changing AUTH_SECRET invalidates existing sessions
steps.expected: A session signed in before the change is no longer accepted after recreation; restoring the key restores normal sign-in.
steps.actual: An existing session answered /api/v1/me 200. After replacing AUTH_SECRET and recreating, the same session answered 401. Restoring the original AUTH_SECRET and signing in again answered 200.

steps.action: Remove the owned fixture and installation projects
steps.expected: Both projects' containers, networks and volumes are removed; nothing else is touched.
steps.actual: docker compose -p doc029-opinstall-r1-fx down -v and docker compose -p doc029-opinstall-r1 down -v exited 0; no containers or volumes remain with either project label. The locally built image tags were left in the cache.

installTiming.basis: Timestamps written by walkthrough-r1.mjs as the commands ran. The interval to readiness includes one failed up caused by the host network pools and the reviewer creating two networks. The build used a warm layer cache from earlier labs of the same revision. The working-installation interval ends at the checks phase; one document check was re-run afterwards because of a checker fault. This is one fast host, not a claim about a cold host or about DNS, TLS and proxy provisioning time.

install.basis: Every V-C44 step passed on its final attempt. Five failed entries are kept: one host-environment failure (address pools) and four reviewer checker faults, each superseded by a recorded retry.

deployment-configuration.failure: With SMTP_URL set and SMTP_FROM unset, the article says email-dependent flows report that email is unavailable. The magic-link request (403) and the password-setup request (503) did report it. An invitation did not: POST /api/v1/auth/invites answered 201, and Settings -> Users -> Invite user -> Send invite closed the dialog and listed the invitee as Invited with no message. No email reached the relay. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md names invites as a flow that reports email as unconfigured, and TECH-011 records that unset SMTP reports unconfigured loudly. Screenshot r1-invite-without-smtp-from.png.
deployment-configuration.otherChecks: All other V-C45 checks passed: restart versus up, upload ceiling and fallback, topology, proxy origin, wrong origin refusal, upload/download and live update through the proxy, local/s3/azure-blob storage with retained readers, storage validation and unreachable reader, engine bounds and unavailable engine, external database and its negatives, environment SMTP pin and removal, no email Settings page, key rotation, wrong/missing/short key and AUTH_SECRET session invalidation.

teardown: Both owned projects were removed with docker compose -p <project> down -v, including the two pre-created networks. The built image tags stay in the local cache. The private clone, .env and fixture passwords were deleted after the run.
limitations: Agent container-operation walkthrough, not a human operator study.
Local HTTPS used Caddy internal CA for openlaw-r1.localhost; public DNS and certificate issuance were not tested.
The app port was published on all interfaces as the article's Compose file does; host firewall rules to restrict direct access were not tested.
A proxy body-size limit was not configured, so matching the proxy limit to MAX_UPLOAD_MB was not exercised.
S3 and Azure used MinIO and Azurite with explicit keys; cloud identity credential chains were not tested.
Signing and AI provider configuration and their outbound traffic were not exercised; C42/C43 remain blocked on real provider access.
The live-update check read the record frame on /api/events in the page; the visible Comments list did not show the new comment within 10 s, likely because the Comments applet was closed.
